own_solution.law: For a source approaching a stationary listener in still air, f_heard = f_emitted c/(c-v_source). Thus 440(343)/(343-20) = 467.244582 Hz. Raising the emitted frequency by 16 Hz gives 456(343)/323 = 484.235294 Hz. Initial distance contributes a constant propagation delay that cancels when calculating frequency.
assumptions: The stated source speed applies during emission of the measured sound.
The emitted frequency remains steady after any tuning is completed.
The ordinary acoustic Doppler model applies.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TEDCB and T62DC replace the specified tuning increment of 16 Hz with an unspecified 'small amount', so the tuning variants do not preserve the same number and unit as required.

notes: The physical problems have unique answers; the invalid verdict concerns the required matching of numerical values across variants. Both distance sentences specify 300 m consistently. Tuning on an earlier run does not alter the explicitly specified 440 Hz frequency at the current switch-on. The timing provisions ensure that current-run siren tuning affects the measured frequency.
